public_interpretation_before: Police-sourced reporting establishes that AI face-swapped card portraits passed online checks in 15 account openings, converting a facial-verification result into consequential account-opening authority for someone other than the cardholder. The same reports establish a separate identity-representation failure: the suspects possessed lost cards bearing identifiable portraits and used those portraits as input for unauthorised AI composites. This class covers requester-side misuse; the generator’s private consent controls need not be identified. The financial activity is reported at syndicate level, so no particular loan or card transaction is assigned to the 15 AI-assisted accounts. Police reporting supports the account-opening and unauthorised likeness mechanisms, while subsequent transactions remain unallocated to the AI-assisted subset. factual_basis_before: The AI Incident Database indexes the case but relies on reporting rather than providing the application files or bank verification logs. HK01’s account of the 19 April 2025 police briefing supplies the application period (March 2024–February 2025), at least 21 lost cards, 44 applications and 30 opened accounts. It distinguishes 15 successful openings involving AI face swapping from other altered-photo methods; all 30 should not be described as AI successes. HK01 reports that investigators received intelligence in February 2025, arrested eight suspected members in April, and described loans and card spending involving approximately HK$860,000 and laundering of more than HK$1.2 million in suspected proceeds. The South China Morning Post independently reports the police briefing and arrests. The exact bank controls, the identity of affected cardholders, final charges or convictions, recoveries, and ultimate allocation of economic loss remain unestablished. A June 2026 Hong Kong Government reply describes a different October 2025 operation with 19 accounts and must not be merged into this occurrence. HK01 specifies 10 April for the arrests. SCMP describes Thursday in the 7–17 April operation; the exact date is not harmonised. The 503 arrests and HK$1.56 billion in the wider operation are not this eight-person case.
